title: Creation Groans
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: Creation's beauty is a faint picture of what will be. We feel the decay, but the Spirit is God's guarantee of our full redemption.
exhortation: Creation is majestic and glorious. You see it when you take a hike or visit some beautiful place. Jonathan and I were recently kayaking down the Colorado River, and it was breathtaking: those amazing canyon walls, and you start thinking about how they were formed.

But it struck me that the beauty we were seeing was created by a massive rift as the earth was torn apart. As beautiful as it is, the canyon is also a testimony to decay and destruction, exactly what this verse is talking about. At one point we heard a loud sound, and rock came crumbling down the canyon wall. We were watching it decay around us.

So creation, as beautiful as it is, is just a glimmer, a faint picture of what was before sin. We can't fathom how beautiful it will be when the full redemption comes. Even creation will be redeemed, and a new heavens and a new earth brought forth.

And we are much the same. "We ourselves, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly as we wait eagerly for adoption as sons, the redemption of our bodies." When we put our faith in Christ, we were given the Holy Spirit, the firstfruits, the guarantee of what is to come. But if you're like me, every year older you're more aware that you are marching toward an earthly death. The decay is real and unavoidable. Many are feeling it in their bodies and don't need to be told.

How faithful of the Lord to give us his Holy Spirit as the promise of the full redemption we will receive in Christ when we receive our heavenly bodies. There is a great hope, Christian. A day of redemption is coming. We have the deposit, and the Lord is faithful to bring us all the way to that glorious end. So take hope in that.
prayer: Lord, as we look at your creation, may we see both its beauty and the marks of judgment, and may that turn us to your grace and mercy. Let us be awestruck not just by creation, but by your great grace displayed on the cross for us.

History is moving toward a moment when everything will change. When you split the clouds and we hear the trumpet sound, sin, decay, death and injustice will be dealt the final blow. May we see the delay as your patience and mercy toward a world that needs your grace, and may we declare your gospel to those around us as we wait for the day you return. We pray this in Jesus' name. Amen.
